question: What is the main job of the human skin when it comes to keeping us healthy?
explanation: Think of the skin as your body's natural raincoat and shield! It stops germs and harmful bacteria from getting inside. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h1)

question: Why should nurses advise against using harsh chemical soaps for a patient's daily bath?

options.B: They strip away protective skin oils

explanation: Harsh soaps wash away the skin's natural oils, leaving it dry, itchy, and easily broken down. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h1)

question: Poor mouth care in hospital patients can lead to which serious lung problem?
explanation: When the mouth isn't kept clean, bacteria can slip down into the lungs and cause a nasty infection called aspiration pneumonia. Good oral care is powerful medicine! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h2)

question: Why is it best for patients to take out their removable dentures at night?

options.A: To prevent the plastic material from melting
options.B: To give the underlying gum tissues adequate rest
options.C: To allow the salivary glands to produce more saliva
options.D: To stop the patient from grinding their teeth

explanation: Just like your feet need a break from tight shoes, gums need a break from dentures to breathe and stay healthy. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h2)

question: What is the golden rule for trimming a patient's toenails to avoid painful ingrown nails?
explanation: Always trim straight across! Cutting down into the corners invites the nail to dig right into the soft skin. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h3)

question: Which group of patients needs the most careful, watchful eye when it comes to foot care?
explanation: Diabetes can affect blood flow and feeling in the feet, meaning small cuts can go unnoticed and turn into major problems. Daily foot checks are a must! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h3)

question: When cleaning a female patient's perineal area, what direction should you always wipe?

options.A: From the urinary meatus toward the anus
options.B: From the anus toward the umbilicus
options.C: In a circular motion starting at the rectum
options.D: From the inner thighs inward to the labia

explanation: Always remember: clean from front to back! This simple habit keeps nasty bowel germs away from the urinary tract. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h4)

question: How should you clean down an indwelling urinary catheter tube?

options.A: Starting near the drainage bag and moving upward
options.B: Starting at the insertion site and moving outward
options.C: Scrubbing vigorously back and forth over the meatus
options.D: Wiping exclusively in tight circles around the collection bag

explanation: Always start right where the tube enters the body and wipe outward. Moving upward would push germs right into the bladder! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h4)

question: What nursing term describes a patient who struggles to do everyday tasks like bathing on their own?
explanation: When someone temporarily or permanently needs help with daily activities like washing or dressing, we call it a self-care deficit. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h5)

question: Why must nurses respect cultural beliefs when planning a patient's personal hygiene?

options.A: Preferences regarding modesty and gender of the caregiver vary widely
options.B: Cultural norms dictate the exact chemical composition of soap
options.C: Medical mandates require identical routines for every human being
options.D: Certain cultures forbid the use of any liquid water for cleaning

explanation: Everyone has different comfort zones when it comes to privacy and who helps them wash. Respecting culture builds great nurse-patient trust. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h5)

question: What is the absolute number one standard precaution before and after helping a patient wash?

options.A: Using sterile surgical gowns for every bed bath
options.B: Restricting all family members from the hospital room
options.C: Applying antibiotic ointment to all skin surfaces
options.D: Performing hand hygiene before and after the procedure

explanation: Good old-fashioned handwashing is your superpower for stopping the spread of hospital infections! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h6)

question: How does letting a hospital patient wash their own face help their recovery?

options.A: It speeds up the metabolism of oral medications
options.B: It guarantees an immediate drop in body temperature
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for professional nursing staff
options.D: It fosters a sense of control and preserves dignity

explanation: Hospitals can make patients feel helpless. Letting them do what they can for themselves boosts their mood and speeds up healing! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h6)
